user_prompt: I was away on a three-week business trip and barely trained. Can I jump straight back into my usual gym routine at the same weights and volume?
ai_response:
After a 3-week break, I wouldn't usually jump straight back into your exact normal loads and volume on day one. You probably haven't lost much muscle, but your work capacity, coordination, and tolerance to heavy training are likely a bit lower.
A good return strategy:

* Week 1 back: Do your normal program, but reduce:
   * Weights: ~80–90% of your usual working loads
   * Sets: ~70–80% of your normal volume
   * Effort: Leave 2–4 reps in reserve (don't grind)
* Week 2: If you feel good (normal soreness, joints feel fine, recovery is okay), return to normal loads and volume.
* Week 3: Push progression again.

For your first session back:

* Warm up a little longer than usual.
* Avoid testing maxes or rep PRs.
* Be cautious with high-fatigue movements (heavy squats, deadlifts, lots of eccentric work) because soreness can hit harder after a layoff.

If your program is something like a strength program where the loads are percentage-based, you can usually just run the next week at a slightly reduced percentage rather than restarting.
Three weeks isn't a long enough break to "start over" — think of it more like a short deload plus a re-acclimation week.
If you tell me your program (e.g., 5/3/1, PPL, upper/lower, bodybuilding split, etc.) and your main goal (strength vs size), I can suggest exactly how to restart it.
